quiz.name: MDC-301 W1 — Introduction to Machine Learning

questions.question: Which three ingredients describe the basic learning setup used in this course?
options: A GPU, Python, and a large dataset
A model family, a loss, and a method for fitting parameters
A training set, a validation set, and a test set
Features, labels, and a graphics card
questions.explanation: A model family supplies candidate rules, a loss measures prediction error, and an optimisation method adjusts model parameters.

questions.question: In machine learning, generalisation means:
options: Performing well on new examples not used to fit the model
Training as quickly as possible
Using every available feature
Producing an explanation for every prediction
questions.explanation: The goal is useful performance on examples beyond the ones used for fitting, not just memorisation of training rows.

questions.question: A model scores 99% on training data but 62% on held-out test data. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Underfitting
Overfitting
Perfect calibration
The test set was used only for plotting
questions.explanation: A large train–test performance gap is evidence that the fitted model may have learned training-specific patterns.

questions.question: A model with 100% training accuracy is necessarily a good model for future examples.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Training accuracy alone does not show how well a model generalises.

questions.question: A model performs poorly on both the training set and the test set. Which diagnosis is most likely?
options: Overfitting
Underfitting
A high test score
Label leakage
questions.explanation: Poor performance even on training examples is consistent with a model that is too simple or otherwise not fitting the task.

questions.question: A system estimates a 0.73 probability that a customer will leave. What kind of task is it solving?
options: Regression, because the probability is written as a number
Classification, because the probability refers to a category
Unsupervised clustering
Reinforcement learning
questions.explanation: A probability can be the output of a classifier; the task is determined by the target category, not by the numeric probability display.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the three broad learning settings introduced in Chapter 1?
options: Supervised learning
Unsupervised learning
Reinforcement learning
Deductive learning
questions.explanation: The chapter introduces supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning.

questions.question: Why keep a test set separate until the final evaluation?
options: So it can be used repeatedly to choose the best model
So it gives a less biased check on data not used for fitting or model selection
So the training set can be deleted
So every model gets a perfect score
questions.explanation: Repeatedly selecting models based on test results leaks information from the test set into the development process.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes regression from classification?
options: Regression predicts a numeric quantity; classification predicts a category
Regression always uses images; classification always uses tables
Regression is unsupervised; classification is supervised
They are different names for the same task
questions.explanation: The target type is the key distinction: a numeric amount versus a class or category.

questions.question: In one word, what should a useful machine-learning model do well on?
